decorative: Front cover: a mosque, palm and tree in a green landscape, coloured letter blocks, the Class 3 badge and the KPTBB logo; "Free from Government — Not for Sale".
A third-party website advertisement (awazeinqilab.com) inserted into the scanned PDF. It is not part of the textbook and is not reproduced.
Title page with coloured "ناظرہ قرآن" lettering, a name-plate frame and the Character Education Foundation logo.
A "PERFECT24U.COM" website watermark is printed across the middle of the scan; it is not part of the textbook and is ignored.

issues: This scan is an exact duplicate of the previous scan (printed page 6, the letter chart); the content is given once on the previous page.

decorative: Each letter is printed in three coloured bubbles (with zabar, zer and pesh). A pupil's pencil marks are visible on the scan and are ignored.
Each card shows the word broken into letters (in pink) above the joined word.
The words are printed in linked pairs of bubbles; each pair contrasts letters with similar sounds.
The letter with jazm (or the qalqalah / hamzah sakin letter) is printed in pink in each word.
The letter with shadd is printed in pink in each word.
The top three rows show linked pairs: a short form (blue) beside the long form (pink, with standing zabar, standing zer or inverted pesh).
The letters of madd / leen are printed in pink in each word.

The words are grouped by arrows to two madd signs: the first group shows madd where a word ending in a madd letter meets a hamzah in the next word; the second shows madd followed by hamzah or shadd in the same word.
The letter carrying tanween is printed in pink in each word.
The letters read with ghunnah are printed in pink in each word.
The mim sakin and the following mim or ba are printed in pink in each phrase.
issues: The book's teaching note says the ghunnah is made on مْ when mim or ba follows; with ba the usual name is ikhfa shafawi (a hidden, nasal mim), and with mim it is idgham shafawi. Both are read with ghunnah, as printed.

decorative: A framed Mushaf page (15 lines) with tajweed words printed in colour, beside a yellow side panel.
issues: Quran text: Indo-Pak script (quran.com). English meaning: M. M. Pickthall (1930, public domain); the book prints no translation, and no verified public-domain Pashto translation is available, so the Pashto slot repeats the Arabic text.
